subject: Pricing handoff: token model + approval path
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@stratatek.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + ask: token volumes / budget / approvers

Hi Alex — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and the asks so we can put together a tight commercial proposal: 

Call recap
- Use case: document summarization and customer-facing chat across web + mobile (latency-sensitive).
- Expected traffic pattern: peak after new product launches, baseline steady-state.
- Models: leaning toward Llama-3-ish open model variants; interested in Redwood Optimize for batching + KV caching.

Open asks for pricing/qualification
1) Target token volume range (monthly): can you confirm a low / mid / high scenario (tokens/month)?
2) Budget range for inference (monthly or annual committed spend): a ballpark helps us propose committed vs. flex pricing.
3) Who is the economic buyer (name + role)? Who signs finance/POs?
4) Any procurement/legal constraints we should know (SLA, audit logs, data residency)?

Next steps
- If you can reply with the three bullets above, we will draft a quote with a recommended $/1M-token unit and a couple of commitment tiers. Attached: simple token model worksheet (token_model_v1.xlsx) — fill if useful.
- I’ll loop in Rishi to propose unit economics and Marissa to confirm billing/contract path.

Thanks — speak soon.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

Attachments: token_model_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@stratatek.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@stratatek.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + ask: token volumes / budget / approvers

Hi Olga — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below: 

1) Token volume (monthly) — rough scenarios
   - Low: 10M tokens/mo (pilot)
   - Mid: 50M tokens/mo (initial production)
   - High: 150M tokens/mo (scale after Q2)

2) Budget — we’re targeting something in the $18k–$30k per month range for production (mid scenario). We have some internal pressure to keep unit $/1M below $1k if possible, otherwise we need stronger ROI proof.

3) Economic buyer / finance approver: Priya Shah, VP Finance (cc’d). Priya handles PO approval; procurement is handled by her team.

4) Procurement constraints: standard master services agreement, SOC 2 required, and we prefer U.S. data residency for production. No special IP terms.

I attached a short note from procurement with expected timelines. Happy to set up a quick intro meeting between Priya and Rishi next week.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product, StrataTek
alex.johnson@stratatek.com
Attachment: procurement_timeline.txt (1 page)

Marissa / Rishi — forwarding Alex’s reply. Key takeaways: mid-case ~50M tokens/mo, target $18k–$30k/mo, finance approver is Priya Shah (VP Finance). Procurement wants SOC 2 + US data residency.

Can you: 
- Rishi: propose a unit price and commitment tiers we can present (including a $/1M target to land within Alex’s expectations). Include recommended ramp and any required SLA/discount callouts.
- Marissa: confirm billing/PO flow (do we need a separate billing contact or billing PO template for enterprises like this?) and if we should route this via sales-assisted quoting.

I’ll draft the initial quote once we have the price bands.

Thanks — Olga

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 08:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap + ask: token volumes / budget / approvers

Thanks for the context — here’s a pragmatic pricing sketch we can use to start the commercial conversation: 

Recommended unit economics (public-facing proposition)
- List: $1,200 per 1M tokens for on-demand (no commitment)
- Mid-commitment (12 months / 12M tokens total): $950 per 1M tokens (10% discount applied for commitment)
- High-commitment (12 months / 100M+ tokens/mo): $800 per 1M tokens (tiered runway discount, requires Dedicated capacity/SLA)

Notes and caveats- At the 50M tokens/mo scenario, the $950 band is defensible if we include batching + KV caching optimizations (Redwood Optimize) and a standard 30-day SLA.
- If StrataTek requires a stricter SLA or custom audit windows, we should account for a one-time engineering onboarding fee or higher list price.
- I’ll prepare a short quote template and attach a draft quote (draft_quote_StrataTek_v1.pdf).

Next actions
- Olga: propose a short call with Priya next week to align on approver timeline and any contract redlines.
- Marissa: flag billing template and confirm whether PO or invoicing cadence preferred (monthly vs. annual upfront).

Happy to hop on a call with Alex + Priya and walk through the unit math.

-Rishi
Director, Commercial Pricing, Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@stratatek.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@stratatek.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Next steps & draft quote attached — request: finance approver confirmation and timeline

Hi Alex / Priya — looping Priya in formally and attaching a draft quote based on our internal pricing sketch. Summary below: 

- Mid-case (50M tokens/mo): recommended list -> $1,200/1M, committed -> $950/1M (12mo, 12M tokens total commitment applied as monthly average). Estimated monthly cost at 50M = $47,500 list / $47,500? Wait, that math is wrong.

[clarification inline]
- Corrected estimate: at 50M tokens/mo, the committed band ($950/1M) yields ~ $47,500/month. If they target $18k–$30k/mo they will need to either (a) take a higher per-token optimization package (larger commitment/ramp), or (b) reduce model selection/throughput profile. Let's discuss which path they prefer.

Attachments: draft_quote_StrataTek_v1.pdf (pdf, draft quote) and token_model_v1.xlsx.

Priya — can you confirm: who signs the PO / how long is procurement review usually (2–4 weeks?) and whether StrataTek requires a purchase order number on monthly invoices? If helpful, we can set a short intro call to walk through the draft SOW and the SLA language Rishi called out.

Alex — if the budget band is firm in the $18k–$30k range, I suggest we prepare an alternative proposal: either a smaller pilot (10M tokens/mo) priced to fit the budget, or a stepped ramp commitment that hits $950/1M by month 3. Which would you prefer to discuss with Priya?

Thanks all — I’ll hold the draft quote pending Priya’s timeline.

Best,
Olga
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
